q: Which movement combined modernist styling with fine craft and rich materials?
n: Art Deco combined modernist geometric styling with fine craftsmanship and rich materials. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Art Deco.

q: What shape is commonly used in architectural design to connote stability, rigidity, and strength?
n: The triangle is a rigid, stable shape (it cannot deform without changing side length), so it connotes stability and strength. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What additive form has secondary forms gathered around a dominant central parent form?
n: A centralized form has secondary forms gathered around a dominant central parent form. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What solid has a square base and four triangular faces meeting at a point?
n: A square pyramid has a square base and four triangular faces meeting at an apex. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What effect can the color red tend to produce on people?
n: Red is an advancing, warm colour that tends to produce excitement and stimulation. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response.

q: What color is restful and warm but should be combined with orange or yellow, as it may produce a depressing effect when used alone?
n: Brown is warm and restful but can feel depressing alone, so it is enlivened with orange or yellow. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response.

q: What centralized, concentrated form is usually stable in its setting?
n: A sphere is a centralized, highly concentrated form, usually stable in its setting. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: Attribute of color that determines the amount or strength of the color.
n: Intensity (saturation or chroma) is the attribute that sets a colour's strength or purity. Source: Munsell Color System; Ching.

q: What scheme uses only one color?
n: A monochromatic scheme uses one hue in various values and intensities. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: What does "polychromatic" mean?
n: Polychromatic means many colours. A polychromatic scheme uses several hues, as opposed to a monochromatic one. Source: Merriam-Webster.

q: What has no saturation and therefore no hue?
n: Achromatic colours (black, white, grays) have no saturation and so no hue. Source: Munsell Color System.

q: Which colors are mixed to make other colors?
n: Primary colours are mixed to make other colours. They cannot be produced by mixing other colours in the traditional pigment model. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Three colors spaced as an equilateral triangle on the wheel form a:
n: Three colours equally spaced on the wheel, an equilateral triangle, form a triad. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Two analogous colors plus their complements form a:
n: Two analogous colours plus their complements form a double-complementary (tetradic) scheme. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Any three adjacent colors on a 12-part wheel are:
n: Three adjacent colours on a 12-part wheel are analogous. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Which scheme uses a base color plus the two colors beside its complement?
n: A split-complementary scheme uses a base colour plus the two colours on either side of its complement. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: What is an arrangement of colors forming an integrated whole?
n: A colour scheme is an arrangement of colours forming an integrated whole. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Designates a color with low lightness and low saturation, reflecting only a small fraction of incident light.
n: A dark colour has low lightness and low saturation and reflects only a small fraction of incident light. Source: Munsell Color System; CIE colour terminology.

q: Which property classifies a color as red, yellow, green, blue or in between?
n: Hue classifies a colour as red, yellow, green, blue or in between. Hue is the attribute named by the colour family, its position on the colour wheel. Source: Munsell Color System.

q: Which property is how light or dark a color appears?
n: Value is how light or dark a colour appears. Adding white raises value to a tint, and adding black lowers it to a shade. Source: Munsell Color System.

q: Color made by mixing cyan, yellow and magenta pigments that absorb wavelengths is:
n: Mixing cyan, yellow and magenta pigments, which absorb wavelengths, is subtractive colour. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, colour mixing.

q: Color made by combining red, green and blue light is:
n: Combining red, green and blue light is additive colour. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, colour mixing.

q: What circular chart shows the hues with complements opposite each other?
n: A colour wheel is a circular chart of the hues, with complementary colours placed opposite each other. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated; Itten, The Art of Color.

q: What warm color seems to move toward the viewer?
n: Warm colours such as red and orange seem to move toward the viewer. They are advancing colours. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response.

q: What phenomenon of light is described by hue, saturation and lightness (or brightness)?
n: Colour is the phenomenon of light described by hue, saturation and lightness (brightness). Source: CIE colour terminology; Munsell Color System.

q: What is the blending of small dots of pure color seen from a distance?
n: Optical mixing is the blending, seen from a distance, of small dots of pure colour, as in pointillism. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, pointillism.

q: What is the appropriate color for fast food?
n: Yellow is associated with energy, cheerfulness and appetite, which is why fast-food branding uses it, often with red. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response; Singh, Impact of Color on Marketing (2006).

q: Which color connotes purity?
n: White connotes purity and cleanliness. It is used in hospitals and clean rooms to suggest hygiene and openness. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response.

q: Which color reflects the most light?
n: White reflects the most light (highest light reflectance value). Source: IES Lighting Handbook (reflectances).

q: Which color has the longest wavelength?
n: Red has the longest wavelength of visible light, about 620–750 nm. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, colour (visible spectrum).

q: Which is NOT a secondary color?
n: Yellow is a primary colour. Orange, violet and green are secondaries. Source: Itten, The Art of Color.

q: What color is often associated with energy and hunger?
n: Yellow is often associated with energy and hunger (appetite stimulation). Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response.

q: Which are the secondary colors?
n: The secondary colours are green, orange and violet, each mixed from two primaries. Source: Itten, The Art of Color.
